name: Blacks Creek Elk Migration
source: Blacks Creek Elk Migration Statistics and seasonal migration routes map, analyzed / prepared by Jodi Berg and Scott Bergen, July 2020
summary: The Blacks Creek-Danskin elk herd winters in the foothills southeast of Lucky Peak Lake in Idaho. During their spring migrations, these elk typically traverse the Middle Fork Boise River and South Fork Boise River using two main migration routes to reach summer ranges much farther up the valleys in the Boise Mountains. They may also travel as far as the Sawtooth Valley. On average, the Blacks Creek-Danskin elk herd travels more than 44 miles to migrate between winter and summer range. Individuals with the longest routes may travel more than 140 miles. The population in the Boise River Elk Zone was estimated to be 8,800 elk in 2021.
methods: Of 92 individual seasonal migrations, 3 used Brownian bridge movement models with an 8-hour time-lag, 30 used forced motion variance (1400 m) models with a 14-hour time-lag, and 59 used force motion variance (1400 m) models with a 27-hour time-lag.
